Application Requirements

Our application process is designed to help us learn about you. Here is what you will need to submit, step by step, whichever application you use, with the dates each part is due and how to send it.

Submitting your application

You may apply using the Common Application. Your application is not complete until we have received every part of it, including the forms your school sends on your behalf. Most parts can be submitted online, and we will confirm receipt by email within a few days.

If you still cannot locate your application confirmation email, please contact us and choose the category Admissions in the drop-down menu, or call our office during business hours.

Fee or fee waiver

The application fee is non-refundable. If the fee presents a hardship for your family, you can request a fee waiver in the application itself, and doing so will never disadvantage your application in any way. Families of every background apply with waivers each year.

Fee waivers are granted for students who receive a College Board fee waiver, an ACT fee waiver, or who are eligible for the federal free or reduced-price lunch program, as well as for many other circumstances that your counselor can describe on your behalf.

Standardized testing

Applicants are required to submit SAT or ACT results. In exceptional cases when those tests are not accessible, other examinations can meet the requirement. You may self-report your scores in the application, and admitted students will later be asked to send official score reports before they enroll.

We accept scores from any test date, and we consider your highest scores. You do not need to send every score you have earned; send the ones that you believe present you best. Scores from tests taken after our deadlines may arrive too late to be considered.

School reports and recommendations

Your school counselor will submit a School Report, which includes a counselor letter and your high school transcript. Two teachers from different academic subjects will submit recommendations. Later in the year your counselor will send a Midyear School Report with your first semester grades.

Admitted students will also have a Final School Report sent once their senior year is complete. If your school cannot submit forms online, your counselor can mail them, and we will match them to your application by name and date of birth as quickly as we can.

Interviews

After you apply, you may be invited to interview with an alumna or alumnus in your area or by video. Interviews are offered as volunteers are available, and not having an interview will not count against you. You will be contacted directly if an interview can be arranged in your area this year.

Interviews are informal conversations meant to help you learn about the college and help us learn about you. There is nothing special you need to prepare, and you are welcome to ask your interviewer anything about their own experiences as a student.

Deadlines

Restrictive Early Action applications are due in early November, and Regular Decision applications are due in early January. Both programs allow you to compare admission and financial aid offers from other institutions and to wait until May 1 to make a final college choice, so there is no reason to rush.

Decisions are released online through the applicant portal. Early applicants hear in mid-December and may be admitted, deferred to the regular pool, or not admitted. Regular applicants hear in late March. Every admitted student receives a financial aid offer at the same time as the decision.

Financial aid

Financial aid is need-based, and admission is need-blind for every applicant, including international students. To apply for aid, submit the CSS Profile and the FAFSA by the same deadlines as your application. Families with lower incomes are expected to contribute nothing toward the cost of attendance at all.

Our net price calculator gives an estimate of what your family would pay in a few minutes. The estimate depends on your family's income, assets, and the number of children in college, and the financial aid office is glad to talk through your own circumstances by phone or email at any time.

Completing the Harvard supplement questions

Complete the Harvard Questions with the Common Application. This includes the following five required short-answer questions, each with a 150 word limit.

  • Harvard has long recognized the importance of enrolling a student body with a diversity of perspectives and experiences. How will the life experiences that shaped who you are today enable you to contribute to Harvard?
  • Describe a time when you strongly disagreed with someone about an idea or issue. How did you communicate or engage with this person? What did you learn from this experience?
  • Briefly describe any of your extracurricular activities, employment experience, travel, or family responsibilities that have shaped who you are.
  • How do you hope to use your Harvard education in the future?
  • Top 3 things your roommates might like to know about you.

What if I am homeschooled?

Homeschooled applicants are treated the same as all other applicants.
